questions.questionText: The law which states that the induced electromotive force (emf) is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation: Faraday's law states that the magnitude of induced emf in a circuit is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit.

questions.questionText: The negative sign in the expression for Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, e = -dΦ/dt, is a statement of:
questions.explanation: Lenz's law provides the direction of induced current such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it, representing conservation of energy.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of magnetic flux Φ is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb), where 1 Wb = 1 T·m².

questions.questionText: The self-inductance L of a coil depends on which of the following factors?

options.text: Geometry of the coil and core permeability

questions.explanation: Self-inductance L is a purely geometric and material property depending on the number of turns, cross-sectional area, length, and core permeability (L = μ₀ μ_r N² A / l).

questions.questionText: Eddy currents are produced in a conductor when it is placed in a:
questions.explanation: Eddy currents are circulating loops of electrical current induced within bulk conductors by a changing magnetic field.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of mutual inductance is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit for both self-inductance and mutual inductance is the Henry (H).

questions.questionText: The motional emf induced across a straight conducting rod of length L moving with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: Motional emf induced across a conductor moving perpendicularly to a magnetic field is given by e = B L v.

questions.questionText: Energy stored in an inductor of self-inductance L carrying a steady current I is:
questions.explanation: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor carrying current I is given by U = 1/2 L I².

questions.questionText: A square loop of side 0.1 m is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field that increases at a uniform rate of 20 T s⁻¹. The magnitude of induced emf in the loop is:
questions.explanation: Area A = (0.1)² = 0.01 m². Induced emf e = A × (dB/dt) = 0.01 × 20 = 0.2 V.

questions.questionText: A conducting rod of length 1 m is rotated about one end with an angular speed of 100 rad s⁻¹ in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. The emf induced between the ends of the rod is:
questions.explanation: Rotational motional emf e = 1/2 B ω L² = 0.5 × 0.2 × 100 × (1)² = 10 V.

questions.questionText: If the current in a primary coil changes from 5 A to 0 A in 0.1 s, an emf of 20 V is induced in the secondary coil. The mutual inductance of the two coils is:
questions.explanation: Induced emf e = M (ΔI / Δt) ⇒ 20 = M × (5 / 0.1) ⇒ 20 = 50 M ⇒ M = 0.4 H.

questions.questionText: An ideal air-cored solenoid of length 0.4 m and cross-sectional area 10 cm² has 800 turns. Its self-inductance is approximately:
A magnetic flux through a stationary loop of resistance 10 Ω varies with time t as Φ = (6t² - 5t + 1) Wb. The magnitude of induced current at t = 0.25 s is:
Two coaxial circular coils of radii r₁ and r₂ (r₁ << r₂) are placed in the same plane with their centers coinciding. The mutual inductance M of the system is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Field at center due to outer coil B₂ = μ₀ I₂ / (2 r₂). Flux through inner coil Φ₁ = B₂ (π r₁²) = (μ₀ π r₁² I₂) / (2 r₂). Thus M = Φ₁ / I₂ = μ₀ π r₁² / (2 r₂), which is proportional to r₁² / r₂.

questions.questionText: A coil of resistance 20 Ω and inductance 0.5 H is connected across a 100 V DC supply. The maximum energy stored in the magnetic field of the coil is:
questions.explanation: Steady-state DC current I = V / R = 100 / 20 = 5 A. Stored energy U = 1/2 L I² = 0.5 × 0.5 × 5² = 6.25 J.

questions.questionText: A wheel with 10 metallic spokes, each 0.5 m long, is rotated at 120 rev min⁻¹ in a plane perpendicular to the horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field B_H = 0.4 Gauss. The induced emf between the axle and the rim is:
questions.explanation: Frequency f = 120 / 60 = 2 rev s⁻¹. Angular velocity ω = 2π f = 4π rad s⁻¹. B_H = 0.4 × 10⁻⁴ T. e = 1/2 B ω L² = 0.5 × (0.4 × 10⁻⁴) × (4π) × (0.5)² = 3.14 × 10⁻⁵ V. (Note: standard spokes in parallel do not change total induced emf across rim-axle).

questions.questionText: A long solenoid of cross-sectional area A and n turns per unit length has a short coil of N turns tightly wound around its center. The mutual inductance between the solenoid and the coil is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic field of solenoid carrying current I is B = μ₀ n I. Flux through secondary coil of N turns is Φ = N (B A) = μ₀ n N A I. Therefore, M = Φ / I = μ₀ n N A.

questions.questionText: A copper ring is held horizontally and a bar magnet is dropped along the axis of the ring with its North pole pointing downward. The acceleration of the falling magnet is:
questions.explanation: As the magnet falls toward the ring, the changing magnetic flux induces a current in the ring which creates a magnetic field opposing the approaching N-pole (Lenz's Law). The upward repulsive force reduces acceleration below g.

questions.questionText: A rectangular loop of dimensions a and b with resistance R is pulled out of a uniform magnetic field B with a constant speed v perpendicular to the field edge. The mechanical power required to pull the loop is:
questions.explanation: Assuming length b is perpendicular to velocity v and crosses the boundary: induced emf e = B b v. Current I = e / R = B b v / R. Magnetic force F = I b B = (B² b² v) / R. Mechanical power P = F v = (B² b² v²) / R.

questions.questionText: A rectangular coil of N turns, area A, and total resistance R rotates with constant angular velocity ω in a uniform magnetic field B. The total charge that flows through the coil during a rotation from θ = 0° to θ = 180° is:
questions.explanation: Total induced charge q = ΔΦ / R = [Φ_initial - Φ_final] / R = [N B A - (-N B A)] / R = 2 N B A / R. Notice that total charge is independent of angular speed ω.
